text:
Winnipeg scored twice in 14 seconds early in the first period, and Vancouver never recovered, falling 6-2 at Canada Life Centre for its fourth straight loss (0-4-0). Alex Iafallo tipped one in on the power play at 3:49, Cole Koepke followed at 4:03 on a shot our numbers gave a 3% chance of going in, and the Jets had the lead they would keep all night. For Viggo Björck, the Jets' eighth overall pick in 2026 out of Djurgårdens IF, the night brought his first NHL point, an assist on Mark Scheifele's second-period goal.

The scoreboard was not flattering the Jets. By expected goals, which measure the quality of chances taken, Winnipeg led 3.49 to 1.65, and our simulation of the game's shots has the Jets winning 81% of the time. They were strongest in the first two periods, outchancing Vancouver 1.27 to 0.36 in the first and 1.59 to 0.57 in the second. Vancouver pushed back in the third (0.72 to 0.64), and Brock Boeser's late goal made it 6-2, but by then the game was long decided. Leevi Meriläinen allowed 2.5 more goals than the shots he faced should have cost, which is the gap between his 23 saves on 29 shots and what an average goalie would have managed. Neal Pionk and Mario Ferraro, both defensemen, scored on a night when the Jets' defense produced offense and gave up little, and Dawson Mercer, a former 18th overall pick, added a goal and an assist.

The Jets finish this one in control, with Mercer named first star. Vancouver stays winless through four games, and a team that gave away the puck 22 times, against 14 for Winnipeg, has a clear place to start cleaning things up.
